clue.text: See man in game with incomplete flush

parts.note: a bishop is one of the pieces in chess

indicators.note: incomplete says the synonym for flush loses its final letter

parts.note: flush in the sense of well off means rich

explanation.surface: Someone at the card table is told to look at a piece while holding a nearly made flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the definition, not a verb telling you to look: a bishop's see is his diocese. 'Flush' suggests poker, but here it means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese or office governed by a bishop, the same area of church jurisdiction.

clue.text: Flatter bottom on perfect back!

parts.note: butt is slang for the bottom or backside

indicators.note: back says the word for perfect is written in reverse

parts.note: pure means perfect, unflawed

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising someone's shapely rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns PURE into ERUP; 'on' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is an idiom meaning to praise them insincerely, to flatter or soft-soap them.

clue.text: Terrifying assassin is terrified inside

indicators.note: inside says the answer is contained within the run of words assassin is terrified

explanation.surface: A frightening killer is himself scared.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'assaSSIN IS TERrified'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening or suggesting evil, so it is frightening or ominous in effect.

clue.text: He talks rubbish prior to a right old upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the whole string is turned upside down, read bottom to top
prior to places the rubbish before the rest of the string

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone who talks nonsense before taking an old right-winger down a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT, A, R and O make ROTARO, which 'upset' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, someone who makes speeches.

clue.text: Primate's role — helping every sinner unto salvation, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: An archbishop describes his job as leading sinners to redemption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which fits the religious surface, but it means a monkey here; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey from South and East Asia, and monkeys belong to the order of primates.

clue.text: Enter do with press card

indicators.note: enter as an instruction means put one thing inside another

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, to con them
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: An instruction to go to a party with a press pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter' tells you to put MEDIA into CON; 'with' is a link. 'Card' means a joker, not a pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing, eccentric person, a joker who makes people laugh.

clue.text: Gallery holding Seurat opening shows discernment

indicators.note: holding says the gallery's name wraps round a letter

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the painter's name

explanation.surface: An art gallery displaying an early Seurat proves it has a good eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's best-known art gallery. 'Opening' takes S, the first letter of Seurat, which 'holding' puts inside TATE; 'shows' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the ability to judge what is fine or appropriate, which is a kind of discernment.

clue.text: Devil's island?

parts.note: the island home of a famous snarling marsupial named after the devil

explanation.surface: A reference to the notorious French penal colony.
explanation.walkthrough: Devil's Island was a French prison colony, but here the devil is the Tasmanian devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial found in the wild only on this Australian island state.

clue.text: Beetle's second hand motor inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for motor goes within the other letters

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a ship's hand
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A Volkswagen Beetle is a used car with a decent engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' and 'second hand motor' suggest the VW car. The 's stands for 'is'; CAR goes inside S and AB.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: First lady included briefly in show

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the first lady's name

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible
inc. is the short form of included

explanation.surface: A president's wife is given a brief part in a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife; it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality clearly.

clue.text: Pentagon losing head is prepared for us duty

indicators.note: prepared in the sense of made ready signals the remaining letters are rearranged
losing head means the first letter of the building's name is dropped

explanation.surface: The decapitated American defence headquarters still gets ready to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' removes P from PENTAGON to leave ENTAGON, which 'is prepared' rearranges. 'For us' is padding for the surface, linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a tax or duty charged on ships' cargo by the ton.

clue.text: It has decreasing usefulness in the home

definitions.text: It has decreasing usefulness in the home

parts.words: It has decreasing usefulness in the home
parts.note: read de-creasing: a household appliance whose job is to take creases out of clothes

explanation.surface: Something around the house is becoming steadily less useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreasing' looks like 'becoming less', but read it as 'de-creasing', removing creases, which is what this appliance does.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron is a domestic appliance that smooths creases from fabric using heat and steam.

clue.text: Counters found in the laboratory?

definitions.meaning: counters as a verb means answers back sharply
glass vessels with long bent necks used for distilling in chemistry

explanation.surface: Tokens or gadgets that turn up in a science lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Retorts are sharp replies that counter an argument, and also long-necked distilling flasks used by chemists.

clue.text: One grand aristocrat the French find vulgar

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a nob is a slang term for an upper-class person
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A lone wealthy French aristocrat is thought coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand comes from slang for a thousand pounds or dollars. 'Find' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means base or low in character, close to vulgar in its older sense of common and coarse.

clue.text: Blair's one MP with an alert air in a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster is a wrecking of things, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is an MP who has a watchful look in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like it should be the definition, but the definition is 'Blair's one': Tony Blair sat in the House of Commons. 'Disaster' is the anagram signal, and the fodder runs on through 'in a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair, a long-serving British MP and Prime Minister, was a member of the legislature, so he is one example.

clue.text: Comes into the house, perhaps

parts.note: a property is one example of what someone receives in a will

explanation.surface: Someone steps into the house, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes into' looks like walking in, but in the sense of receiving an estate as heir.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is to receive it as an heir from someone who has died.

clue.text: Note sound of pulse after headache

indicators.note: after places the sound-alike piece behind the note

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: sound of says a word for pulse is heard rather than written

parts.note: pulses such as lentils are edible seeds, grain

explanation.surface: Feeling your pulse throb after a bad headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' gives GRAINE, sounding like grain. 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat but means edible seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring headache, often with nausea and visual disturbance.

clue.text: At home with work, setter's idle

parts.note: in means at home
an act is a deed, a piece of work
setter's here means setter has, the setter speaking as I've

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is lazing at home when meant to be working.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to themself: 'setter's' is 'setter has', I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working or not in use, which is inactive.

clue.text: Almost gone gaga with inert gas

indicators.note: gaga means crazy, so the letters are scrambled into a new order
almost means the word gone loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gone senile from breathing inert gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts GONE to GON, and 'gaga' rearranges GON with INERT. 'Inert gas' looks like the definition, but only 'gas' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless, largely unreactive gas that makes up most of Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Clasp of huge bra's undone

indicators.note: undone as in unfastened signals that the letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A large brassiere has come unfastened.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'bra's' stands for 'is' and adds no letter; 'undone' rearranges HUGE and BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a tight, enveloping embrace, a powerful clasp in the arms.

clue.text: A light pulse having ingested carbon monoxide

indicators.note: having ingested means the legume swallows the formula letters

parts.note: a bean is a pulse, an edible legume seed
CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide

explanation.surface: A gentle heartbeat after breathing in toxic gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat; it means a bean, which takes in CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire or lamp set up as a warning or guide.

clue.text: Little money on account causes stress

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed below, so the coin comes under the abbreviation

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: A small sum added to an account brings on worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Causes' is the link. 'Stress' means emphasis on a syllable, not anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the emphasis placed on a syllable in speech.

clue.text: Hot air from explosive on a street

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Empty talk produced by a device going off on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot air' looks like something literally released by a blast; here it means pompous talk. 'From' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated language with little substance, which is what hot air means as an idiom.

clue.text: One's a pretentious person backing oriental art

indicators.note: backing means the whole string is reversed

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a snob is a pretentious person

explanation.surface: Someone who supports Eastern art is a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: I, A and SNOB make IASNOB, which 'backing' reverses; 'backing' looks like supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots.

clue.text: World cover-up by military intelligence on uranium?

parts.note: MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5
a lie is a cover-up of the truth
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Spies conceal a global uranium secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' and 'on' are links; MI is the familiar abbreviation from MI5 and MI6, the British intelligence services.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a social environment or setting, someone's world or surroundings.

clue.text: Sack race isn't a fix

indicators.note: sack in its sense of pillage or ruin signals the following letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A sack race is said not to be rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack race' reads as one thing, but 'Sack' is the anagram indicator acting on RACE ISN'T A.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something such as a date or position is to establish or determine it definitely.

clue.text: Initially sea sick on board ship?

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word sea

parts.note: ailing means sick or unwell

explanation.surface: Someone is seasick from the start of a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose definition: being on board a moving ship is to be under way at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing means travelling by sea on a vessel, the state of being aboard a ship that is under way.

clue.text: Those against taking time in minutes

indicators.note: taking means holding a letter inside, so the opposing voters wrap round it

parts.note: the noes are those who vote against a motion

explanation.surface: The opposition in a meeting takes up time over the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link to the definition. 'Minutes' looks like units of time, but means the written record of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes are the written record kept of a meeting, a set of jottings from it.

clue.text: He appreciates a nice pure spread

indicators.note: spread out means the letters are laid out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man enjoys a pleasant, unadulterated spread on his bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like food to be appreciated; it is the anagram indicator on A NICE PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person devoted to refined enjoyment of good food and drink, a connoisseur of pleasure.
